target.title: fix(scripts): bound ghsa-patch git operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where git operations in the ghsa-patch script could hang indefinitely during security advisory patching. When git commands encounter network issues or repository corruption, `execFileSync` calls would block without any timeout, stalling automated GHSA remediation workflows.

## Why This Change Was Made

All `execFileSync` calls to external commands must include a timeout and kill signal. Without these, transient git issues cause resource leaks and indefinite stalls. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation).

## User Impact

GHSA patching can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when git operations are unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `GHSA_PATCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ??` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/ghsa-patch.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `execFileSync("git", ...)` call, injected a `git` shim that blocks forever, and verified the script exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-ghsa-patch-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: execFileSync("git", [...])
fixture: git waits forever
timeout: GHSA_PATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: git ...
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached.
